exposure: Low-lying placenta (LLP) detected early in pregnancy
outcome: Persistency of low-lying placenta to delivery
cohort: The study included 236 women with low-lying placenta (LLP) detected during an early anatomic scan performed at 13-16 weeks gestation.
finding: Persistent low-lying placenta has unique clinical characteristics and more complications compared to cases that resolved, and its persistency can be predicted with 90.3% accuracy as early as the beginning of the second trimester using a linear support vector machine classification model.
gest_age: LLP detected at 13-16 weeks gestation, with resolution assessed at 22-24 weeks and 36-39 weeks
